skill.name: youtube-content-research
skill.description: Research YouTube videos through SocialDataX keyword searches, filters, and pagination, then organize evidence for content planning and competitor comparisons.
skill.summary: Find YouTube content samples and separate observed evidence from research judgments.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: The 34 static alerts concern Markdown backticks, provider links, declared credential usage, and readable multilingual text rather than demonstrated attacks. A separate medium-severity concern is automatic execution of an unpinned npm package in the credential-bearing runtime. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, destructive operations, or prompt injection in the reviewed files; the external package implementation was not provided.

remediation.issue: The documented npx command automatically runs the mutable latest release of an external package.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and verify package provenance before execution. Use an isolated runtime with only the required API credential.

content.user_title: Research YouTube Content with Focused Video Searches
content.value_statement: Content planning requires relevant video samples and traceable evidence. This skill guides SocialDataX searches and organizes results for topic exploration and competitor comparisons.
actual_capabilities: Search YouTube videos by keyword using the SocialDataX CLI or its corresponding youtube_search_videos MCP tool.
Filter searches by publication time, duration, and video type, with relevance, recency, view-count, or rating sorting options.
Collect bounded samples with page counts, item limits, and opaque continuation tokens.
Organize available titles, authors, links, content identifiers, metrics, and publication dates into traceable research notes.
Separate visible evidence from judgments and suggest follow-up research questions.
Preserve partial results and resume eligible searches within the original page and item budgets.
limitations: Requires SocialDataX access and a configured SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY; direct CLI execution also requires Node.js, npm, and network access.
API calls may require account credits, and service availability affects results.
Search is not exhaustive, and the skill does not provide stable complete-result boundaries or built-in historical trend tracking.
The documented workflow searches videos; it does not retrieve transcripts, log into accounts, or perform posting and engagement actions.

use_cases.title: Explore Video Topics
use_cases.description: Collect a small set of videos around a proposed topic and identify useful follow-up questions before planning a new video.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitor Content
use_cases.description: Search brand and competitor keywords, then compare visible titles, authors, and content angles while preserving source links.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Content Samples
use_cases.description: Filter a topic to recent publication windows and summarize observed themes without presenting a limited sample as a complete market trend.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Find a Small Sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Find one page of YouTube videos about [topic]. Show available titles, authors, and links, then suggest two follow-up questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a focused content research session.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Filter Recent Videos
prompt_templates.prompt: Research [topic] videos published this month and under four minutes. Sort by recency, cap results at 20, and distinguish evidence from interpretation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a bounded set of recent short videos.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Compare Two Brands
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare YouTube search samples for [brand A] and [brand B]. Use identical filters and ten results each. Cite sources and explain sampling limits.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Resume Partial Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume this partial YouTube search: [prior query, results, counts, token, limits]. Preserve collected evidence and original filters. Continue only within remaining budgets.
prompt_templates.scenario: Recover incomplete research without restarting the first page.

output_examples.input: Find one page of beginner photography videos and explain which results deserve closer review.
output: Illustrative format only; no live search was performed.
Sample entry: returned video title, author, source link or identifier, and publication date when available.
Evidence: describe the visible title or description supporting relevance to beginner photography.
Judgment: explain whether the sample merits closer review without claiming to have watched the video.
Follow-up: narrow the search to camera settings, lighting, or composition.

output_examples.input: Summarize an interrupted search while preserving the original collection limits.
output: Illustrative format only; no live search was performed.
Status: incomplete results; retain collected samples and the returned error.
Continuation: use a nonempty returned token with the original filters after resolving the error.
Budget: subtract collected pages and items from the original limits before continuing.
Boundary: do not restart automatically when the continuation token is empty.

best_practices: Start with one page and focused keywords, then expand only when the initial samples justify more requests.
Keep source links and available metadata, and label interpretations separately from observed evidence.
Use a reviewed, pinned CLI release and keep API credentials out of prompts, reports, and shared logs.
anti_patterns: Treating search samples as exhaustive coverage or proof of audience demand.
Repeating failed searches after insufficient balance or restarting partial searches without checking continuation rules.
Claiming transcript analysis, video viewing, or account actions from a search-only workflow.

faq.question: What inputs does the skill accept?
faq.answer: Provide a keyword or topic direction. Optional search settings include publication time, duration, video type, sorting, page count, and item limits.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Configure SOCIALDATAX_API_KEY for provider access. The direct CLI needs Node.js, npm, and network access; an already configured MCP tool is another documented option.

faq.question: Can searches incur charges?
faq.answer: Yes, SocialDataX calls may consume account credits. The workflow stops repeated retries for insufficient balance and directs users to the provider billing page.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my YouTube account?
faq.answer: The documented workflow is read-only. It does not log in, post, like, comment, or change account settings.

faq.question: Can it retrieve every matching video?
faq.answer: No. Search lacks a stable complete-result boundary. Use page and item limits, and do not assume one empty page means no further results.

faq.question: What happens when a search returns partial results?
faq.answer: Keep the collected items and error. Resume with a nonempty continuation token and reduced remaining limits after resolving the problem.
